items.title: Skip placeholder and FALLBACK screens when creating bars
items.body:
## Summary

When monitors sleep or are unplugged, Qt substitutes a nameless placeholder screen and Hyprland creates its headless `FALLBACK` output. A bar built for either outlives the monitors' return: the compositor drops it onto whichever monitor comes back first, where it stacks over that monitor's bar with duplicate `ShellIpc` handlers and leaked child processes (#13072).

This filters out nameless and `FALLBACK` screens in `BarModel.realScreens`, ensuring bar surfaces are only created for real outputs with confirmed geometry.

Fixes #13072

## Testing

- Updated `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh` with assertions for screen filtering.
- Ran `bash test/shell.d/bar-test.sh` (all 98 assertions pass).

items.title: Scale the clock panel hero text with fontScale
items.body:
## Summary

With `[font] base-size` below 12, the clock panel's hero date is clipped by the card's border — at `base-size = 9` (fontScale 0.75) "September 26" renders as "September 2" plus a cut-off glyph (#13381).

The card sizes itself through `panel.fittedContentWidth(Style.space(560))`, and `Style.space()` tracks `fontScale` (`spacingScaleWithFont` defaults to `true`), so at `base-size = 9` the card drops 560 → 420px while the hero stayed at 52px.

This scales the hero date and its decorative glyph with `Style.fontScale` using the codebase's standard `Math.max(1, Math.round(...))` idiom. The glyph/date ratio stays deliberately outside the `Style.font.*` scale — both now track the card that contains them instead.

At the default `base-size = 12`, `fontScale` is exactly 1, so rendering is pixel-identical there.

Fixes #13381

## Testing

- `test/shell.d` has no clock-panel geometry tests; the full suite was previously run on this tree with only the known environment failures (missing `omarchy-pkgs` checkout).
- Rendering is provably unchanged at defaults (`fontScale == 1`); visual verification at `base-size = 9` per `agents/skills/visual-verification.md` on a dev-linked session is recommended — the change is inert there and needs no capture.

items.title: Scale clock panel hero date with fontScale
items.body:
## Summary

With `[font] base-size` configured below 12 (the default), the clock panel scales down via `Style.space(560)` (and `effectiveSpacingScale`), but the hero calendar glyph (48px) and date string (52px) remained hardcoded numbers outside the scale. In months with longer names (e.g. "September"), the text overflowed the narrowed card width and clipped against the right border.

This scales both the decorative calendar icon and hero date string using `Style.fontScale` (`Math.max(1, Math.round(size * Style.fontScale))`). At default `fontBaseSize = 12` (`fontScale = 1.0`), the rendered pixel sizes are completely unchanged (48 and 52), while at smaller or larger base sizes they scale in exact proportion with the popup card.

Fixes #13381

## Testing

- `bash test/shell.d/clock-test.sh`: all tests pass, including new assertion verifying that the hero date and glyph scale with `Style.fontScale`.
- `./test/cli`: passed.

items.title: Skip placeholder screens when building bars
items.body:
Fixes #13163

## Problem
With every monitor unplugged (e.g. a KVM switched to another machine), `Quickshell.screens` briefly holds screens that aren't real monitors:
- Qt's nameless **placeholder screen** (`There are no outputs - creating placeholder screen`)
- Hyprland's headless **`FALLBACK`** output

The bar's `Variants { model: Quickshell.screens }` built a full `BarPanel` for each of them. When the real monitors came back, the compositor dropped that orphaned bar onto the first monitor to return, stacked over its own bar, and the second monitor had no bar until the real ones finished building.

## Change
- `BarModel.js` gets `isRealScreen()` / `realScreens()`: screens with a name that isn't `FALLBACK` and a non-zero size. It uses the same test `plugins/lock/Service.qml` uses in `realScreenCount()`, plus the `FALLBACK` exclusion.
- `Bar.qml`: `readonly property var realScreens: BarModel.realScreens(Quickshell.screens)`, and the bar, `DragGhostPanel` and `BarMoveGhostPanel` `Variants` all use `root.realScreens`.
- Qt names a screen before adding it, so only its size can arrive late. Those size reads are tracked by the binding, so a screen whose size lands afterwards still gets its bar.
- `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh`:
  - Node checks of `isRealScreen()` / `realScreens()` against a nameless 0x0 placeholder, `FALLBACK` at 1920x1080, a real monitor, a user-created `HEADLESS-N` output, an unsized screen and missing input.
  - Source checks that no bar `Variants` uses `Quickshell.screens` directly, that all three use `root.realScreens`, and that it comes from `BarModel.realScreens`.

## Verification
Intel N150, two 4K HDMI monitors through a KVM. I polled `hyprctl layers -j` every 0.5 s across repeated switch-backs:

| after switch back | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| first bar | +1.6 s (the orphaned bar) | +1.1–1.3 s (real HDMI-A-1 bar) |
| both monitors have their bar | +6.3 s, with HDMI-A-1 showing **2** | +2.0–2.3 s, never more than 1 per monitor |

I checked with logging in the shell that no `BarPanel` was created for the placeholder or `FALLBACK` (`realScreens` stayed empty while only those existed).

## Tests
- `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh`: all 97 checks pass. The new checks fail on `quattro` without this change. I also broke the fix three ways (letting `FALLBACK` through, pointing one `Variants` at an unfiltered list, making `realScreens` bypass the filter), and each one fails a check.
- `./test/shell`: 7 of 252 files fail, **identically on unmodified `quattro`** on this machine. They're environment-dependent (no `omarchy-pkgs` checkout, no `omasnap`, kernel/snapper migration tests), plus `runtime-smoke-test.sh`'s "IPC handler once per screen (saw 4 for 2 screens)", which fails the same with and without this change. The smoke test loads the shell from this branch with the same 12 passing checks as on `quattro`.

## Out of scope
- Tested on the 4.0.4 shell with this patch applied, since the `Variants` blocks are identical there; not on a full `quattro` install.
- `plugins/lock/Service.qml`'s `realScreenCount()` still counts `FALLBACK` as a real screen. Left alone to keep this PR to the bar.
- Correction to #13163: the per-widget costs there came from a build that logged every widget slot, which inflated them about 2–3×. Uninstrumented, a bar builds in about 1.3 s on this machine.

items.title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
items.body:
On some machines the EC reports a bogus but numeric current. My MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI+ (BAT1 BIF0_9) reports current_now=-65A for a ~7.5W discharge, so the panel showed Discharging -1124W while UPower correctly reported 7.5W.

The sysfs override only guarded readability, so any numeric value clobbered the good UPower rate. This:

- only trusts sysfs reads that succeed and are numeric (allows negative current_now, which is the normal discharging sign),
- rejects insane magnitudes (>150W) or values wildly above UPower's rate (>3x when UPower is solid), keeping the UPower value instead,
- displays the rate as magnitude (state already says charging/discharging, so no more -1124W),
- compares idle against magnitude so a large negative rate can't fake charge-idle,
- omits cycle_count 0 when UPower reports charge-cycles N/A so the panel shows — instead of a misleading 0.

Complements #12649/#12755 (those cover failed/empty reads); this covers bogus-but-numeric reads. Verified with the extended battery-status-test.sh scenarios (bogus -65A, non-numeric, sane negative discharge) plus live hardware: bogus -1113W discharge now shows 7.5W, and a sane 29.1W charge still uses the live sysfs value.

items.title: Keep UPower rate when sysfs power reads fail or are non-numeric
items.body:
Fixes #12735.

## Problem
`omarchy battery status` shows `0W` while discharging, even though UPower knows the real rate (time-left is correct, only wattage is wrong). On affected machines `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/power_now` exists, so `[[ -r ... ]]` passes — but the read itself fails with `ENODEV`, leaving an empty value that `awk` turns into `0`, clobbering the good `5.5W` from UPower. Same hazard in the `current_now`/`voltage_now` branch.

## Change
- `bin/omarchy-battery-status`: only override the UPower rate when the sysfs read actually succeeds and is numeric (`cat ... 2>/dev/null` + `^[0-9]+$` guard, as suggested in the issue), for both the `power_now` and the `current_now`/`voltage_now` branches. Otherwise the UPower value stands.
- `test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh`: two new scenarios — a `power_now` node whose read fails (fake `cat` refusing `power_now`, standing in for the ENODEV kernel read) and a non-numeric `current_now` — both asserting the UPower rate survives.

## Verification
- `bash test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh`: pass (new assertions included)
- Negative control: the new assertions fail against the pre-fix script (`not ok - battery status keeps the UPower rate when power_now fails to read`) and pass with the fix
- `./test/all`: CLI suite fully green; shell suite shows only the 5 pre-existing environment failures (missing `omarchy-pkgs` checkout, `omasnap`, Qt portal) — confirmed identical on the clean tree

# [Intel Mac P02] Repair headers for retained stock kernels

Carry the existing omacom/omarchy#12074 migration that installs missing stock-kernel headers when broadcom-wl-dkms is present, including retained fallback kernels. The production migration is unchanged; local additions are fixtures.

**Draft consolidation for source review and hardware-owner follow-up.** Known defects remain; no hardware or merge-readiness certification is claimed. Part of the [14-feature Intel Mac series](https://github.com/andrew-boyd/omarchy/blob/intel-mac/review-index/INTEL-MAC-ROLLUPS.md) with three package companions.

**Contribute:** open follow-up PRs in `andrew-boyd/omarchy` with base **`intel-mac/p02-kernel-headers`**. Use `[Intel Mac P02]` in the title and a contributor branch such as `intel-mac/p02/describe-change`. Link this feature in the series index. Merging a follow-up into this branch updates its roll-up.

This existing draft: [https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12680](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12680).

## Full Intel Mac scope and current revision

The project covers **all 64-bit Intel Macs: pre-T1, T1 and T2**. MacBookPro13,3 is only the first available physical test machine. Each feature has its own hardware boundary; one model's success does not validate the rest.

Candidate head: `803260c8feff6d9ed5dbac60d5f630cd45ae1b56`; reconciled upstream: `8f324c90b82790d31ab33565441e07cbdb8d2308`. Published contribution commits and author/co-author metadata remain in the history.

**Ready for attended physical testing; Mac hardware remains untested by this effort.** The reconciled combined ISO passed fresh unencrypted/encrypted VM installations, desktop/password-lock checks, strict Neovim startup/theme checks, synthetic Apple EFI preservation through a disk wipe, and affected package/DKMS/migration checks. ISO SHA-256: `9e6288ef5cc1eadce519cdd7384c8030286eb938a6288eb218f025a61b433252`.

[Exact sources, results, retained failures and reproduction](https://github.com/andrew-boyd/omarchy/blob/intel-mac/review-index/hardware-test/HANDOFF.md). These results cover the pinned combined image; [standalone-versus-combined differences](https://github.com/andrew-boyd/omarchy/blob/intel-mac/review-index/hardware-test/receipts/integration-coverage.json) remain explicit. The inventory now records 188 source/context PRs: 101 have dispositions in feature tables and 87 remain only in separate work tracks. **This is not 188 implemented PRs or 188-to-14 compression.** The 14 feature PRs and three package companions remain the published coordination targets; retained backlog is not claimed complete.

items.title: Keep UPower rate when sysfs power read fails with ENODEV
items.body:
Single-battery HP/ACPI machines expose a `power_now` that passes `[[ -r ]]` but whose `read()` fails with `ENODEV`, so the script gets `""` and `awk` coerces it to `0W`, discarding UPower's correct `energy-rate` (~16-30W).

Only trust numeric sysfs reads, otherwise keep UPower's `energy-rate`. Same guard for the `current_now`/`voltage_now` fallback, which had the identical coerce-to-0 hole.

Split out from #6845 per @bjarneo's request — that PR grew to cover 3 failure modes and was closed as a dup of #10392, which only handles multi-battery percentage and keeps this bug. This is the minimal fix for #6895 with regression tests for both empty-read cases.

Fixes #6895.
Extracted from #6845 (`3c40745`).

Verified: existing `battery-status-test.sh` + 2 new ENODEV cases pass.

The 4.0.3 upgrade swapped `broadcom-wl` for `broadcom-wl-dkms` without headers on stock `linux` (older MacBooks). The module never built, so Wi-Fi died after reboot.

Install matching headers in `fix-bcm43xx.sh`, and repair existing DKMS installs with a migration that covers `linux` / `linux-lts` as well as Omarchy/T2 kernels.


items.title: Install stock kernel headers for broadcom-wl-dkms on upgraded Macs
items.body:
Arch dropped the prebuilt `broadcom-wl` on 2026-09-02, and `broadcom-wl-dkms` carries `replaces=(broadcom-wl)`. On an upgrade, pacman swaps the package in and pulls `dkms`, but nothing pulls `linux-headers`, so the module never builds:

```
running '70-dkms-install.hook'...
==> ERROR: Missing 7.2.3-arch1-3 kernel headers for module broadcom-wl/6.30.223.271.
```

2012-2015 MacBooks with a BCM4360 or BCM4331 then come back from the Quattro upgrade with no driver bound and no Wi-Fi device at all. The installer's `fix-bcm43xx.sh` never runs on those machines, and `1789444024` only covers `linux-omarchy` and `linux-t2`.

`1789325478` will give `linux-omarchy` its headers, but it deliberately leaves the stock kernel installed as the boot fallback. On these Macs that fallback still has no Wi-Fi, which is usually the way back to a working system.

This migration installs headers for any installed Arch kernel (`linux`, `linux-lts`, `linux-zen`, `linux-hardened`) when `broadcom-wl-dkms` is present. The dkms pacman hook triggers on `usr/lib/modules/*/build/include/`, so installing the headers builds the module.

## Testing

- `test/shell.d/broadcom-wl-headers-migration-test.sh` covers the repair, idempotency, leaving `linux-omarchy` to its own migration, skipping machines without `broadcom-wl-dkms`, and propagating a failed install. It fails when the install line is removed.
- `test/shell.d/kernel-headers-migration-test.sh` and the other migration tests still pass.
- Verified on a MacBook (BCM4360, `14e4:43a0`) upgraded to 4.0.3 on stock `linux` 7.2.3. Installing `linux-headers` built `wl` through the hook, `modprobe wl` brought up `wlp3s0`, and NetworkManager connected.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fixes #10975
